title: Does scheduling operating tests shorten verified recovery?
question: With the same fixed reader, reset capability, production objective and exogenous inputs, how do planned consecutive load tests affect observed recovery, methane, ending reserves and costs?
rationale: Compare the existing opportunistic probe policy with explicit requested/delivered-power hypotheses, consecutive confirmation, an earliest-feasible test objective, a battery reserve and an observed-failure retry interval. This changes a complete recovery policy package, including forward accounting for accepted service demands and stricter confirmation. It does not isolate only the optimiser or make global service-routing choices.

service_economics.basis: Illustrative EUR assumptions; procurement at upstream release, with no refund for rejected deliveries. No actual vendor invoices.

smoke.purpose: Exercise multi-arm execution, cancellation, preservation and reporting; too short for recovery-value conclusions.

reference.purpose: Descriptive three-seed recovery comparison over three solar cycles.

sensitivity.purpose: Longer follow-through with plant capacity, battery headroom and observation-noise sensitivity. Other capacities, hardware and recovery assumptions remain fixed unless the variant changes them explicitly.

comparison: Scheduled-test policy minus opportunistic-probe policy, matched by condition, variant and seed. Only complete matched physical traces enter differences. Undefined prices and absent recovery confirmations are excluded separately for the affected metric with explicit available-pair counts; they are never filled with zero. Failed/incomplete cases and all attempts remain visible.
policy_tuning: The methane objective, fixed service hardware and local service-task rule are shared. The candidate adds scheduled-load-tests/1, strict consecutive confirmation, forward accounting for accepted service demands and its frozen recovery assumptions. This is a prospective package comparison without training or case-specific tuning. It is not a general joint mission scheduler.

resolution.plant_basis: Reference or active-run plant, production costs, sensors, process implementation choices and solar design. The protocol supplies service hardware, logistics, service prices and challenge settings; every replacement of an active-run value is recorded.
resolution.variants: Apply declared numerical scales, then replacements, then the condition; explicit tier hours, horizon, solver budget and seed apply last. No implicit capacity scaling of hardware or inventory. Named solar capacity factors also scale every section and converter of an explicit active design; converter fractions change only the converter. All resolved values are retained.
resolution.arms: Separate runs with one frozen controller policy each. Arm patches may change service machinery, thresholds and prices, but not shared plant/weather/fault inputs or the common environmental-loss model.
resolution.weather: Saved synthetic reference and forecasts. Each matched group must have identical weather bytes. Wind and rain for work eligibility are explicitly assumed, not site observations.
resolution.faults: Persistent module damage or a resettable module trip begins at hour 10, except the no-fault control. There is no flow-sensor bias in this protocol. No fault clears merely because a timer elapsed; reset is incompatible with module damage. Injected cause and successful repair truth are unavailable to both controllers.
resolution.randomness: Named sensor channels and exogenous seed are matched. Both arms freeze target-action-request/1: accepted request ordinals match each target/action independently. Different accepted workloads can alter their observations and outcome sequence; evaluation never grants future realised draws to a planner.
resolution.costs: All service assumptions are frozen; allocated period cost, action-dependent cost and modelled expenditure remain distinct. This protocol retains the version-1 comparison boundary: calendar maintenance allowance only, with executed routine maintenance and dock standby explicitly disabled. Dedicated support studies vary those assumptions.
resolution.terminal: Count the complete run including startup. Keep battery, gas, thermal state, robot energy, usable supplies, completed-unverified and unfinished work. No sale proceeds or credit for postponing work. Extended sensitivity windows expose boundary dependence.

metric_definitions.methane_kg: Sum of applied methane; hydrogen inventory is separate.
metric_definitions.total_eur: Allocated plant and service period cost; undefined if an applicable price is missing.
metric_definitions.service_expenditure_eur: Modelled service billings and procurement events; not total plant cash flow or invoices.
metric_definitions.human_work: Site visits, actual committed crew hours and remote hours are separate.
metric_definitions.recovery: Physical restoration is the first hourly truth boundary back at nominal capacity after a derating. Confidence is the next decision boundary after a post-restoration observation restores the capacity estimate, following an earlier estimated derating. Delay is undefined if either event is absent. Probe hours count requested tests; deadline misses and candidate solves apply only to the scheduled policy and are undefined for its baseline.
metric_definitions.terminal: All ending inventories and service state retained; unfinished and completed-unverified orders reported separately.

checks: Independent physical, service-resource and three-view economic audit for every complete arm
Identical matched weather hashes and exogenous input signatures
Preserved protocol, original prices, source, attempts and numerical rerun differences
Explicit incomplete data, solver limitations, unsupported prices and unfinished work
limits: Illustrative hardware, procedure reliability, sensor models, tracking hypotheses, reserves, retry timing and prices; no empirical reliability or economic calibration.
Three seeds provide descriptive comparisons, not population confidence intervals.
This comparison changes a recovery-policy package. Stricter confirmation, service-demand anticipation and scheduling need later ablations before any gain is attributed to a single mechanism.
Both arms use the same fixed contact reader and reset interface, with no mobile robot or human replacement. Persistent module damage can therefore remain unresolved.
Earliest feasible tests have explicit recovery priority. Production, operating contribution and ending reserves can worsen; no improvement is required.
Short windows do not establish annual installation economics. No soiling removal occurs; both arms retain the same environmental-loss mechanism.
The protocol retains calendar maintenance allowances while executed routine maintenance and dock standby are disabled. These available mechanisms require separate declared experiments.
Delivery profiles are hypotheses, not guarantees. Actual execution may reject a requested test, break its confirmation sequence and defer a retry.

review.scope: Prospective scheduled-recovery comparison, revision 1. The two policy definitions, same-information boundaries, opt-in semantics and reporting timestamps were reviewed against the implementation. No numerical outcome is claimed by this protocol. Future parameter changes require a new edition.

interpretation_rules: No requirement that scheduled tests improve methane or cost. Earliest feasible testing is a recovery-priority objective, not a calibrated value of information.

Physical restoration and post-restoration confidence are separate; confirmed time is the next decision boundary after an observed update. A never-restored or never-confirmed case has undefined delay, not zero.
A module-damage fault cannot be fixed by a reset. The shared baseline has no human replacement; unresolved faults and test retries remain outcomes.

Tracking/unchanged-delivery probabilities, reserve fraction and retry interval are explicitly illustrative policy assumptions. Neither planner receives injected fault identity or a successful-repair draw.
This is a package comparison: stricter consecutive tests, future accepted service demand and scheduling change together. Add ablations before attributing benefit to one mechanism.
Short windows do not settle annual economics. Report ending inventories and unfinished verification alongside output, service/decision costs and solver limits.
